title: H-1B Visa Holders Face Gruelling 30-Minute Interviews at Hyderabad Consulate
excerpt: Consulting and staffing company employees report intensive questioning sessions lasting up to 30 minutes at the US Consulate in Hyderabad, as eliminated dropbox waivers, social media vetting, and a backlog stretching to 2027 reshape the visa stamping process.
body:
• Consulting and staffing company employees at the US Consulate in Hyderabad now face interviews lasting 10 to 30 minutes, with officers probing end-client relationships, project details, and reporting structures — far longer than the 3- to 5-minute sessions for direct hires.
  • Since September 2025, every H-1B applicant in India must attend an in-person interview — dropbox waivers and third-country stamping options have been eliminated.
  • Social media vetting introduced in December 2025 has added a new layer of scrutiny: private profiles on LinkedIn, Instagram, or X trigger immediate 221(g) administrative processing.
  • H-1B appointment slots at all five Indian consulates are booked until mid-2027, with major employers including Apple and Google issuing internal "do not travel" advisories to visa-holding staff.

An H-1B visa holder who recently attended a stamping interview at the US Consulate in Hyderabad described a gruelling 30-minute session that included detailed questioning about their consulting company arrangement, end-client project, salary, social media presence, and reporting structure — a sharp contrast to the quick approvals that once defined the process.

The account, shared on immigration forums and corroborated by immigration attorneys tracking Hyderabad interview patterns, reflects a broader shift at the consulate that has turned routine visa stamping into an extended interrogation for thousands of Indian IT professionals.

Why Hyderabad Is Ground Zero

Since 2023, all first-time H-1B visa stamps for Indian nationals happen exclusively at the Hyderabad consulate, regardless of where the applicant lives in India. The $297–340 million complex in Nanakramguda, the Financial District, is the largest US visa processing facility in South and Southeast Asia, with 54 interview windows and capacity for 3,500 applicants daily.

Officers at Hyderabad see IT professionals all day and know the patterns. For direct-hire employees at companies like Google, Amazon, or Microsoft, interviews typically last 3 to 5 minutes — standard verification questions about salary, job title, work location, and educational qualifications. Consulting and staffing company employees face a fundamentally different experience: 8 to 15 probing questions over sessions stretching 10 to 30 minutes.

"If you work for a consulting company, expect longer interviews. Officers dig into the client relationship — client name, location, project details, reporting structure, and why the work can't be done from India."

— Permito.ai, H1B Visa Stamping Hyderabad 2026 Guide

What Officers Ask Consulting Employees

Immigration attorneys and recent applicants report a consistent pattern of deep probing for consulting-model H-1B holders. Beyond standard questions about employer name, salary, and work location, officers now routinely ask:

Who is the end client? Where is the client located? How large is the company? Can the applicant produce a client letter on the client's letterhead? What specific products or projects does the applicant work on? How many H-1B employees does the sponsoring company have? And the question that trips up many applicants: why does this work require physical presence in the United States?

Officers cross-reference verbal answers against the Labor Condition Application, I-129 petition, and DS-160 form in real time. Any inconsistency — a different salary figure, a mismatched city, a job title that does not align with the petition — triggers deeper scrutiny or a 221(g) administrative processing hold.

The New Scrutiny Layers

Three policy changes since late 2025 have compounded the pressure on applicants. On September 2, 2025, the State Department ended broad interview waivers, eliminating the pandemic-era "dropbox" system that had allowed many H-1B renewals to skip in-person interviews entirely. Age exceptions for applicants under 14 and over 79 were also removed.

Four days later, on September 6, third-country stamping ended for Indian citizens, closing off Canada, Mexico, Dubai, and Singapore as alternatives. All demand now funnels through just five Indian consulates.

Then on December 15, 2025, consulates began checking applicants' social media profiles — X, Facebook, Instagram, YouTube, TikTok, and LinkedIn — during interviews. Private or restricted profiles trigger immediate 221(g) holds. Immigration attorneys advise making all profiles public at least two weeks before an appointment and ensuring LinkedIn work history matches DS-160 entries exactly on dates, titles, and company names.

A Backlog Stretching Into 2027

The cumulative effect of these changes has created an unprecedented appointment crisis. All five US consulates in India — Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, Hyderabad, and Kolkata — show no regular H-1B interview slots available through the end of 2026, with the next realistic appointments pushed into mid-2027.

The State Department's official wait time of approximately 75 days for H/L visas at Hyderabad is, according to multiple immigration law firms including Morgan Lewis, Reddy Neumann Brown, and Seyfarth Shaw, "dangerously misleading." Major employers have responded accordingly: Apple and Google sent internal advisories in December 2025 telling visa-holding employees not to leave the United States for non-essential travel, warning they could be stranded abroad for 12 to 18 months or longer.

"Only travel for stamping if you have a confirmed appointment and your employer's immigration counsel has approved the trip. Have a contingency plan."

— Permito.ai advisory for H-1B holders

The Consulting Company Squeeze

The intensified interview process hits Indian IT consulting firms hardest. H-1B approvals for Indian IT consulting companies have fallen 70 percent from FY2015 levels. In FY2025, the top seven Indian IT firms received only 4,573 primary H-1B approvals — Amazon alone secured 4,644.

Under revised lottery rules announced by USCIS on December 29, 2025, the system now weights salary and experience levels, with Level IV (expert) workers receiving four lottery entries compared to one for Level I (entry-level) positions. The shift further disadvantages consulting firms that historically placed junior professionals.

What Applicants Can Do

Recent applicants who navigated the process successfully at Hyderabad share consistent advice: arrive 90 minutes early, keep documents organized with DS-160 and appointment letter together and passport, I-797, and LCA on top. Consulting employees should know their end client inside out — company name, location, project specifics, and the name of their manager at the client site.

For those who receive a 221(g) hold, Hyderabad uses color-coded slips: green for missing documents (1 to 4 weeks resolution), blue for background checks (3 to 6 months), white for internal review (the most common), yellow for fraud detection (rare), and pink for document verification. Cases referred to Washington can take 12 months or longer.

The $100,000 supplemental fee introduced for new H-1B petitions where the beneficiary is outside the US — effective since September 21, 2025 — does not apply to renewals, extensions, or employer transfers. The proclamation expires September 21, 2026, unless extended.
nri_angle: Indian IT professionals in the US face heightened risks when traveling to India for H-1B stamping, with major employers advising against non-essential travel and appointment slots unavailable until mid-2027.
